title: Would XENONnT and PandaX-4T have seen it? Expected high-energy counts in their published regions of interest
question: How many events would XENONnT (3.1 t yr) and PandaX-4T (1.54 t yr) contain under LZ's best-fit models (L10 1000 GeV; O1 inelastic delta=250/300/350 keV, each normalised to 1.0 LZ event) inside their published ROIs and if extended to 270 keV?
headline_result: Combined XENONnT+PandaX-4T expect 0-0.23 events for ROIs ending at <=100 keV (zero for delta>=300 keV) but 1.5 events (P(0)=22%) with LZ-like 270 keV ROIs; their 2025 null results are uninformative
key_numbers: L10 XENONnT/PandaX: 0.074/0.037 (<=55 keV), 0.15/0.08 (<=100), 0.34/0.17 (<=150), 1.02/0.51 (270); inelastic onsets 55/91.5/155 keV; combined 270 keV: 1.53 ev, P0=0.216; xenon world 7.48 t yr mu=2.63, P(exactly 1)=0.19; 90% chance of >=1 (>=3) events needs 7.0 (16.1) t yr at 270 keV
model_or_mechanism: xenon-target universality of dR/dE; efficiency folding; L10 = dipole-dipole q^2 O4 - m_N^2 O6 (WimPyDD, validated vs digitised LZ Fig. 1)
builds_on: LZ arXiv:2609.02823 (Table I, Figs 1/S2, Table S7); dossier 00; anticipates P003
agent_tools: Read x19, Bash x17, Write x8, Edit x6
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; WimPyDD 2.0.4; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1; matplotlib 3.11.2; common/lzcommon.py
local_inputs: fulltext.tex (Intro refs, Table I, Fig 1/6/S2/S7 captions, SM, Table S7); Fig1 and FigS2 PNGs; dossier; dossier_numbers.json; lzcommon.py; WimPyDD/package.py (read-only)
recalled_knowledge: 9 items: exposures 3.1 and 1.54 t yr (certain); XENONnT/PandaX ROI edges (uncertain); Anand L10 reduction, NREFT response structure, drift fields, SHM conventions (likely); 0.9 in-ROI efficiency (assumption)
